module_title: Personal Assistance Tasks and Administrative Support

lessons.title: Managing Correspondence and Email Overload
lessons.body: As a personal assistant in Africa, you will handle email for busy executives who receive 100+ messages daily. Start by setting up filters in Gmail or Outlook. For example, create a label 'Urgent' for emails from the boss's spouse or key clients, and auto-forward invoices to a 'Finance' folder. Use tools like Boomerang or FollowUpThen to schedule remindersâfree versions work. A practical rule: check email three times a day (9am, 1pm, 4pm) instead of constantly. In your first week, ask your client which senders are VIPs. Draft template replies for common requests: meeting confirmations, 'I'll get back to you,' and payment acknowledgements. Save these in a Google Doc or Notion page. For WhatsApp, which is huge in Africa, use the 'Archive' and 'Pin' features. If your client gets 50 WhatsApp messages a day, you can respond to simple ones like 'What's the address?' with a saved location pin. Always confirm receipt within 2 hours during work hours. For physical mail, scan important documents using a phone app like CamScanner and email them to the client. Keep a log of all correspondence in a simple spreadsheet: Date, Sender, Subject, Action Taken, Status. This prevents missed follow-ups. If you're in Nigeria or Kenya, expect many emails about invoices and mobile money payments (M-Pesa, Flutterwave). Learn to spot phishingânever click links from unknown senders. Finally, set an out-of-office reply when your client travels. A good assistant reduces email volume by 40% within a month by unsubscribing from newsletters and delegating routine replies.

lessons.title: Scheduling Appointments and Making Reservations
lessons.body: Scheduling is the backbone of a PA's job. Use Google Calendar or Calendly to avoid double-booking. For a client in Lagos, you might manage 15 appointments a week. Always confirm time zonesâAfrica has multiple (WAT, EAT, SAST). When booking a doctor's appointment at a private hospital like Aga Khan in Nairobi, call ahead and ask for the doctor's secretary's direct line. For restaurant reservations, use apps like OpenTable or call directly. In Accra, for a business lunch at Santoku, book 3 days ahead. For travel reservations, use local platforms: Travelstart for flights, Booking.com for hotels. Always get a confirmation number and save it in a shared Google Sheet with columns: Date, Time, Location, Contact, Confirmation #. Send a reminder to your client 24 hours before via WhatsApp and email. For recurring meetings, set up a Zoom link and test it 30 minutes prior. If a client is running late, call the other party to rescheduleâdon't just text. For personal appointments like salon visits, use Fresha. Keep a buffer of 30 minutes between meetings. If you're in South Africa, use SnapScan for parking payments. Always ask: 'What is the cancellation policy?' For flights, note that Ethiopian Airlines and Kenya Airways have different baggage rules. Use TripIt to organize itineraries. Finally, keep a 'waitlist' for popular restaurantsâcall at 5pm for last-minute cancellations. A good scheduler saves a client 5 hours a week.

lessons.title: Bill Paying and Basic Bookkeeping for Clients
lessons.body: Handling bills requires accuracy. Start by listing all recurring bills: rent, electricity (e.g., prepaid meters in Nigeria), water, internet (MTN, Safaricom), DSTV, security, and school fees. Use a simple spreadsheet with columns: Bill, Amount, Due Date, Paid Date, Method, Receipt #. For mobile money, use M-Pesa, Airtel Money, or MoMo. Pay bills 3 days early to avoid disconnection. For electricity, buy tokens via apps like Quickteller or Kuda. Keep all receiptsâscan them into a folder like 'Client X - 2025 Bills'. For bookkeeping, use Wave or Zoho Books (free versions). Record every expense: date, description, amount, category. If your client gives you a petty cash of 50,000 Naira, track every naira. Reconcile weekly: compare your records with bank statements. For invoices, use tools like Invoice2go. If a client owes a vendor, follow up politely: 'Just checking on payment for Invoice #123.' For tax, in Kenya, KRA has iTax; in Nigeria, FIRS. You don't need to file, but keep records for 5 years. For personal bills like school fees, pay via bank transfer and get a stamped receipt. Never mix client money with your own. Use a separate wallet or account. If you're paying cash, get a signed receipt with the vendor's name and phone number. At month-end, produce a one-page summary: total spent, categories, and any unpaid bills. This builds trust. A good bookkeeper saves a client 10% on late fees.

lessons.title: Travel Planning and Itinerary Management
lessons.body: Travel planning for an African executive means handling visas, flights, and ground transport. Start 4 weeks ahead for international trips. For a trip from Johannesburg to London, check visa requirements (UK visa takes 3 weeks). Use Google Flights to compare prices, but book via the airline directly or a reputable agent like Flight Centre. For intra-Africa flights, use Kenya Airways, Ethiopian, or RwandAir. Always book refundable fares if possible. Create a detailed itinerary in Google Docs with: flight numbers, times, hotel addresses, and emergency contacts. Share it with the client and their family. For airport transfers, pre-book Uber or Bolt, or use local services like Little Cab in Kenya. In Lagos, use LagRide. For hotels, choose ones with free cancellation and good security. In Nairobi, the Sarova Stanley is popular. Pack a travel kit for your client: adapters, SIM cards (Airtel or MTN), and local currency (e.g., 200 USD worth). For visas, use VFS Global or TLScontact. Keep digital and physical copies of passports, yellow fever cards, and travel insurance. For long trips, schedule rest days. Use TripCase or TripIt to send alerts. If a flight is delayed, rebook immediately via the airline app. For ground transport in rural areas, hire a trusted driverâask other PAs for referrals. Always have a backup plan: if a flight is cancelled, know the next available. After the trip, file all receipts for expense reports. A good travel PA saves 20% on travel costs by booking early and using loyalty points.

lessons.title: Event Planning and Coordination
lessons.body: Event planning for a PA can range from a 10-person dinner to a 200-person conference. Start with a budget. For a corporate event in Nairobi, expect to spend 2,000 KES per person for a sit-down lunch. Use a checklist: venue, catering, AV, invitations, decorations, and transport. For venues, check hotels like Radisson Blu or local gardens. Always visit the venue and take photos. For catering, get quotes from 3 vendors. In Lagos, use Eventful or Eat.Drink.Lagos for referrals. For invitations, use WhatsApp groups and Evite. Send reminders 1 week and 1 day before. For AV, hire a technicianâtest microphones and projectors 2 hours before. For decorations, use local florists and fabric markets (e.g., Balogun Market in Lagos). For a 50-person event, you need at least 2 helpers. Assign roles: registration, ushering, and food service. Keep a master timeline: setup 3 hours before, guest arrival, speeches, meal, and cleanup. For payment, use mobile money or bank transferânever cash without a receipt. After the event, send thank-you notes within 48 hours. Collect feedback via Google Forms. For virtual events, use Zoom or Google Meet and do a dry run. Always have a contingency: extra chairs, umbrellas, and a first-aid kit. A good event PA can handle 3 events a month and still keep the client calm.

lessons.title: Gift Shopping and Personal Shopping Services
lessons.body: Gift shopping requires knowing the recipient's tastes. For a client's spouse's birthday, ask about favorite colors, scents, and sizes. In Africa, thoughtful gifts include: a bespoke Ankara outfit (from a tailor in Accra or Lagos), a spa voucher (e.g., at Serena Hotel), or a gourmet hamper from local delis. Budget: 20,000-50,000 Naira for a nice gift. Use online stores like Jumia, Konga, or Takealot. For personal shopping, get the client's measurements and preferred brands. For a business wardrobe, shop at stores like Zara or local boutiques. Always keep receipts and ask about return policies. For grocery shopping, use apps like Glovo or Mr D. For a weekly grocery run, expect to spend 30,000 KES in Nairobi. For gifts, wrap them nicelyâuse local artisans for custom wrapping. If you're shipping, use DHL or local couriers like G4S. For last-minute gifts, consider digital options: Spotify gift cards, Netflix, or mobile data bundles (e.g., 10GB from MTN). For corporate gifts, order branded items like notebooks and pens from local printers. Keep a gift log: recipient, occasion, gift, cost, date. This prevents duplicates. For personal shopping, always confirm the budget and style before buying. Send photos for approval before purchase. If you're in South Africa, use Mr Price or Woolworths. For luxury items, use boutiques in Sandton. A good personal shopper saves a client 5 hours a week and avoids gift disasters.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Personal Assistance Tasks and Administrative Support

In African markets, a personal assistant (PA) or errand professional is often the operational backbone of a busy executive, entrepreneur, or diaspora client. The role blends discretion, speed, and financial accuracy. This module gives you the practical systems to manage correspondence, schedule appointments, pay bills, plan travel, coordinate events, and handle personal shoppingâwith Africa-specific tools and safeguards.

Managing Correspondence and Email Overload

African clients often operate across email, WhatsApp, SMS, and phone calls. Your job is to create a single source of truth. Use a shared inbox or label system (Gmail labels: Action, Waiting, Archive, Client Name). Set a triage rule: respond within 2 hours to urgent items, same day to routine items, and flag anything requiring the client's personal decision. Draft template replies for common requestsâmeeting confirmations, payment reminders, and travel queriesâso you are not rewriting from scratch. For WhatsApp, use starred messages and labels; for email, use filters and canned responses. Never delete a client instruction without archiving it. In low-bandwidth areas, use offline mode in Gmail and download attachments before travelling.

Scheduling Appointments and Making Reservations

Time zones matter: Lagos is WAT (UTC+1), Nairobi is EAT (UTC+3), Johannesburg is SAST (UTC+2), and Cairo is EET (UTC+2). Always confirm the client's time zone before booking. Use Calendly, Google Calendar appointment slots, or a shared calendar with colour codes: green for confirmed, yellow for pending, red for conflicts. For reservationsârestaurants, hotels, flightsâbook directly where possible and request written confirmation via email or SMS. In Africa, popular booking platforms include Jumia Travel, Booking.com, and local hotel WhatsApp numbers. Always capture: date, time, location, contact person, confirmation number, and cancellation policy. Send the client a calendar invite plus a WhatsApp summary 24 hours before.

Bill Paying and Basic Bookkeeping for Clients

This is where trust is won or lost. Use a simple ledger (Google Sheets or Excel) with columns: Date, Payee, Amount, Currency, Method, Reference, Receipt Attached, Category. In Africa, payments may be made via M-Pesa, MoMo, Paystack, Flutterwave, bank transfer, or cash. For each payment, obtain a receipt or transaction message and save it in a shared folder named by month. Never use personal funds without written approval. Reconcile weekly. If the client has multiple currencies (e.g., USD, NGN, KES), record the exchange rate used and the source. For basic bookkeeping, track income and expenses, categorise by type (travel, office, personal, utilities), and produce a monthly summary. Use tools like Wave (free accounting) or Zoho Books if the client needs more structure.

Table 1: Common bill payment methods in Africa and their documentation requirements
Method Typical Countries Documentation Required Risk Note
M-Pesa Kenya, Tanzania, DRC, Mozambique SMS confirmation + transaction code Confirm recipient name before sending
MoMo (MTN) Ghana, Uganda, Rwanda, Cameroon App screenshot + reference ID Watch for SIM swap fraud
Paystack / Flutterwave Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa Email receipt + dashboard export Use business accounts only
Bank transfer All PDF proof of payment Verify account details by callback
Cash All Signed petty cash voucher Never pay cash without a witness

Source: GSMA State of the Industry Report on Mobile Money, 2024; Central Bank of Kenya payment statistics, 2024.

Travel Planning and Itinerary Management

An African PA must plan for visa requirements, yellow fever certificates, and airline baggage rules that vary by carrier. Build a master itinerary in Google Docs or Notion with sections: flights, accommodation, ground transport, meetings, emergency contacts, and documents. Include airline PNR, hotel confirmation, driver name and number, and local embassy contact. For multi-country trips, check visa-on-arrival eligibility and transit rules. Book airport transfers in advanceâUber and Bolt operate in major cities, but in smaller towns arrange a trusted local driver. Always share the itinerary with the client and a secondary emergency contact. Print two copies: one for the client, one for you.

Event Planning and Coordination

Whether it is a board meeting, a product launch, or a family celebration, use a checklist-based approach. Start with: objective, date, venue, budget, guest list, vendors, and run-of-show. In Africa, venue booking often requires a deposit via mobile money or bank transfer; get a written contract. Confirm catering, AV, and security separately. Create a vendor contact sheet and a minute-by-minute run sheet. Assign a point person for each task. On the day, arrive early, test Wi-Fi and power backup, and keep a printed guest list. After the event, send thank-you notes and collect receipts for reconciliation.

Gift Shopping and Personal Shopping Services

Personal shopping requires knowing the client's preferences, sizes, and budget. Keep a client profile note: favourite brands, sizes, allergies, and gift occasions. For gifts, consider local artisan markets (e.g., Maasai Market in Nairobi, Makola Market in Accra, Rosebank Africa Craft in Johannesburg) for unique items. For online shopping, use Jumia, Konga, Takealot, or Amazon with a local address. Always send a photo of the item before purchase if the client is not present. Keep receipts for returns. For corporate gifts, order in bulk early and confirm delivery dates.

â ï¸ SAFETY WARNING: Financial and Identity Fraud

Never share your client's banking passwords, OTPs, PINs, or full card details with anyoneâincluding someone claiming to be from the bank. Always verify payment requests by calling the client on a known number. Be alert to SIM swap fraud, fake invoices, and WhatsApp impersonation. If a request feels urgent or unusual, stop and confirm. Use two-factor authentication on all financial accounts. Report any suspected fraud immediately to the client and local authorities.

quiz.q: What is a recommended frequency for checking email to manage overload?
options: D) Only when the client calls
quiz.explanation: Checking email three times a day (e.g., 9am, 1pm, 4pm) reduces constant distraction and improves focus.

quiz.q: Which tool can be used to schedule reminders for emails?
quiz.explanation: Boomerang is an email plugin that allows you to schedule reminders and follow-ups.

quiz.q: In Africa, which messaging app is commonly used for business communication?
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp is widely used across Africa for both personal and business communication.

quiz.q: What should you do with important physical mail?
options: C) Keep it in a drawer
D) Give it to the client immediately
quiz.explanation: Scanning important documents with apps like CamScanner allows for digital storage and easy sharing.

quiz.q: What is a key benefit of using filters in email?
options: B) It automatically organizes emails into folders
quiz.explanation: Filters help categorize emails, so urgent messages are seen first and routine ones are filed away.

quiz.q: Which app is recommended for scheduling appointments?
quiz.explanation: Calendly is a popular tool for scheduling appointments and avoiding double-booking.

quiz.q: When booking a doctor's appointment, what should you ask for?
options: B) The doctor's secretary's direct line
quiz.explanation: Having the secretary's direct line makes future scheduling easier and faster.

quiz.q: What is a good buffer time between meetings?
quiz.explanation: A 30-minute buffer allows for travel, preparation, and unexpected delays.

quiz.q: Which platform is useful for organizing travel itineraries?
quiz.explanation: TripIt automatically organizes flight, hotel, and car rental confirmations into a master itinerary.

quiz.q: What should you always get when making a reservation?
quiz.explanation: A confirmation number is proof of booking and helps resolve any issues later.

quiz.q: Which mobile money service is popular in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: M-Pesa is a leading mobile money service in Kenya and other African countries.

quiz.q: How many days early should you pay bills to avoid disconnection?
quiz.explanation: Paying 3 days early ensures the payment clears before the due date.

quiz.q: What is a recommended free bookkeeping tool?
quiz.explanation: Wave offers free invoicing and accounting software suitable for small-scale bookkeeping.

quiz.q: Why should you keep receipts for 5 years?
quiz.explanation: Tax authorities often require records to be kept for several years for audit purposes.

quiz.q: What should you never mix?
options: A) Client money and your own money
quiz.explanation: Mixing funds can lead to accounting errors and loss of trust.

quiz.q: How far in advance should you start planning an international trip?
quiz.explanation: Starting 4 weeks ahead allows time for visas, flights, and accommodations.

quiz.q: Which app is useful for airport transfers in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Little Cab is a Kenyan ride-hailing service commonly used for airport transfers.

quiz.q: What should you include in a travel kit for your client?
quiz.explanation: Adapters and local SIM cards are essential for connectivity and device charging abroad.

quiz.q: What is a good way to handle a flight delay?
options: B) Rebook immediately via airline app
quiz.explanation: Rebooking quickly via the app can secure the next available flight before others.

quiz.q: What is a key first step in event planning?
quiz.explanation: A budget determines all other decisions and prevents overspending.

quiz.q: How many helpers are recommended for a 50-person event?
quiz.explanation: At least 2 helpers can manage registration, ushering, and food service effectively.

quiz.q: When should you send thank-you notes after an event?
quiz.explanation: Prompt thank-you notes show appreciation and professionalism.

quiz.q: What is a good contingency item for an outdoor event?
quiz.explanation: Umbrellas provide shade or rain protection, ensuring guest comfort.

quiz.q: What should you do before buying a gift for a client's spouse?
quiz.explanation: Knowing their preferences ensures the gift is thoughtful and appropriate.

quiz.q: Which online store is popular in Nigeria for gifts?
quiz.explanation: Jumia is a leading e-commerce platform in Nigeria with a wide range of gift items.

quiz.q: What should you keep for every gift purchase?
quiz.explanation: Receipts are needed for returns or exchanges and for expense tracking.

quiz.q: What is a good digital gift option?
quiz.explanation: Mobile data bundles are instantly delivered and useful for many recipients.

quiz.q: Why keep a gift log?
quiz.explanation: A gift log helps you remember what you gave and prevents giving the same gift twice.

quiz.q: What should you do before purchasing personal shopping items?
quiz.explanation: Confirming budget and style ensures the client is satisfied with the purchase.

quiz.q: Which app is useful for grocery shopping in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Glovo operates in several African cities and offers grocery delivery services.
